newsitem.title: USA: Nintendo boosts U.S. game shipments.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo boosts U.S. game shipments.

text.p: Nintendo Co Ltd said Thursday that it will ship 1.2 million units of its new 64-bit game system to the United States by the end of the year, up from a previous projection of 500,000.

Since the U.S. launch of the Nintendo 64 game system late last month, 460,000 units have been sold of 550,000 shipped, according to a statement issued by Nintendo of America, the Japanese company's U.S. unit.
Nintendo of America executive vice president Peter Main said retailers probably could sell between 1.5 million and 2 million game units by the end of the year."
"This new figure will go a long way to meet demand, but shortages may continue in some areas of the country," he said.
He said the game shipments will made on "consistent allotments" through the end of the year.
The company said eight games for the new machine would be available by Christmas rather than the 12 anticipated previously.
The new cartridge game device, which has richer graphics and allows faster play than the older Super Nintendo Entertainment System, was launched June 23 in Japan, a year behind schedule.
The game machine, which retails for about $200, is the latest entry in a fiercely competitive market battle that also includes Sony Corp's Playstation and Sega Enterprises Ltd's Saturn device.
